extra.message: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) via Jinja2 — course_jinja_cast_382 — Full remote code execution on the server via Jinja2 template injection; attacker can read files, execute commands, and pivot to the database. [verified: User-controlled `fragment` concatenated into `Template("Result: " + fragment).render()` with no sanitization; `_wrk_gate` does not neutralize the injection.]

Jinja2 server-side template injection in internal ops endpoint — If the internal ops token is compromised or bypassed, an attacker achieves remote code execution on the server. [verified: User-controlled `fragment` concatenated into `Template("Result: " + fragment).render()` with no sanitization; `_wrk_gate` is auth, not input control.]

OS Command Injection via ping — course_shell_probe_400 — Full remote code execution on the host operating system with the web server's privileges; attacker can read files, install backdoors, or pivot to internal networks. [verified: `host` from request.GET concatenated into `_os.system("ping -c 1 " + host)` with no shell escaping or input validation.]

Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) via Jinja2 with user-controlled fragment — Remote code execution via Jinja2 template engine, full server compromise. [verified: User-controlled `fragment` concatenated into `Template("Result: " + fragment).render()` with no sanitization.]

OS command injection via unsanitized host parameter in ping — If the internal ops token is compromised or bypassed, an attacker achieves remote code execution on the server host. [verified: `host` from request.GET concatenated into `_os.system("ping -c 1 " + host)` with no shell escaping or validation.]

Missing rate limiting on login allows credential brute-force — Attacker can brute-force user passwords through repeated login attempts with no slowdown or lockout, compromising any account with a weak password. [verified: login_view at /accounts/login/ has no rate-limiting decorator, middleware, or custom attempt-tracking; codebase-wide grep for ratelimit/throttle/axes/lockout returns zero matches. Unlimited POSTs enable credential brute-force.]

SSRF via Webhook Delivery — Outbound Request to Inadequately Validated Target URL — Attacker who controls a webhook record can cause the server to make HTTP requests to internal network services, cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), or other internal infrastructure, enabling information disclosure and potential lateral movement. [verified: The WebhookForm.clean_target_url blocks only localhost/127.0.0.1/::1/.internal/.local but not private IPs (10.x, 192.168.x, 172.16-31.x) or decimal/hex-encoded IPs, and urllib.request.urlopen follows redirects by default. A staff-level attacker can create a webhook with a target URL pointing to or redirecting to internal services/cloud metadata.]

SSRF via insufficient webhook URL validation allowing internal IPs — Authenticated staff users can probe internal network services, cloud metadata endpoints, and potentially access sensitive internal resources through webhook delivery. [verified: Identical SSRF gap: clean_target_url() permits private IPs and 169.254.169.254 (AWS metadata endpoint); a staff user can configure a webhook targeting cloud metadata, and deliver_webhooks.py will issue a real HTTP POST to that address, enabling credential theft from metadata services.]

SSRF via Webhook Target URL with Incomplete Hostname Blocklist and Redirect Following — Attacker with staff role can probe internal network services, access cloud metadata endpoints to steal IAM credentials, scan internal infrastructure, and exfiltrate student PII (emails, course codes, submission statuses) from webhook payloads. Responses from internal services are stored plaintext in the database. [verified: WebhookForm.clean_target_url() blocks only localhost/127.0.0.1/::1/0.0.0.0 and .internal/.local hostnames but permits RFC 1918 private IPs and 169.254.169.254 (cloud metadata), and request.urlopen at deliver_webhooks.py:80 follows redirects by default; the code itself admits 'production deployments should also enforce egress controls at the network layer,' confirming the validation is incomplete a]

CSV formula injection via unsanitized assignment titles in grade exports — When a school admin opens the exported grades CSV in a spreadsheet application, injected formulas can execute arbitrary commands or exfiltrate data from the admin's machine. [verified: export_grades_csv writes s.assignment.title directly via writer.writerow with no formula-injection sanitization; the Assignment.title field imposes no character restrictions, allowing an instructor to embed '=cmd|...' payloads that execute on the admin's spreadsheet application.]

CSV formula injection — unsanitized cell values in grade/submission exports — Arbitrary command execution via Excel/DDE when an administrator opens exported CSV files containing formula-injected assignment titles or course codes. [verified: All three export views write course codes and assignment titles (both attacker-controlled via instructors/admins, unvalidated for formula characters) directly to CSV cells; no sanitization wrapper, middleware, or form clean exists to neutralize formula injection.]

CSV formula injection in grade and submission exports via unsanitized assignment titles — Code execution on the administrator's machine when opening exported CSV files in spreadsheet software; could drop malware or exfiltrate data. [verified: Assignment titles are written unsanitized to CSV in export_grades_csv and export_submissions_csv; the title field (max_length=200 CharField) has no regex or exclusion for '=', '+', '-', '@', so an instructor can inject full DDE formula payloads executed when a school_admin opens the CSV.]

CSV formula injection in grade/submission/progress exports — When a school_admin opens the exported CSV in a spreadsheet application, injected formulas can execute arbitrary commands (DDE), exfiltrate data, or establish network connections to attacker-controlled servers. [verified: export_grades_csv, export_submissions_csv, and export_progress_csv write assignment titles and course codes (attacker-controlled CharFields with no character restrictions) directly to CSV cells via csv.writer without sanitizing formula-injection characters; an instructor-planted title like '=cmd|\'/c calc\'!A0' triggers DDE when the admin opens the CSV in a spreadsheet.]

Path traversal: arbitrary file write via unsanitized 'ref' parameter in course_vault_stash_234 — Arbitrary file write to any location writable by the Django process; could overwrite critical files or plant malicious content. [verified: `ref` from request.GET used in `BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json"` with no `../` sanitization, allowing arbitrary file writes.]

Path Traversal — Arbitrary File Write via name parameter — course_dock_shelf_389 — Arbitrary file write of attacker-controlled binary content; can overwrite critical application files, deploy webshells, or corrupt the system. [verified: `name` from request.GET used unsanitized as file path; `request.body` written to attacker-controlled location.]

Arbitrary file write via unsanitized name parameter — Attacker can write arbitrary files (web shells, cron jobs, config overrides) anywhere the web server user has write access, enabling code execution. [verified: `name` from request.GET is used as `BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name` with no path-traversal sanitization, and `request.body` bytes are written to the attacker-chosen path.]

XML External Entity (XXE) Injection via lxml — course_xml_fold_452 — Arbitrary local file disclosure (e.g., /etc/passwd, .env, source code), server-side request forgery to internal services, and potential denial of service via billion laughs attack. [verified: lxml parser with dangerous flags parses untrusted `request.body`, enabling XXE file disclosure and SSRF.]

XXE via insecure lxml parser configuration in course_xml_fold_452 — Arbitrary local file read (e.g., /etc/passwd, .env, database credentials) and potential SSRF through DTD network access. [verified: lxml parser with `resolve_entities=True, load_dtd=True, no_network=False` parses untrusted `request.body`, enabling XXE attacks.]

Account Enumeration via Distinct Disabled-Account Login Error — Attacker with breached credential pairs can confirm which accounts exist in the system with valid credentials, even when disabled. Facilitates credential stuffing and targeted re-enablement attacks. [verified: Same code path as idx 0 — the distinct error branch at line 24-25 is reachable whenever authenticate() returns a user (is_active=True, correct password) but is_disabled=True. No rate-limiting, CAPTCHA, or lockout neutralizes this enumeration vector.]

Account enumeration via distinct disabled-account error message — An attacker can compile a list of valid user accounts in the system to target in further attacks. [verified: Same as idx 0-2: LoginForm.clean() reveals the disabled state through a unique error string. No middleware, decorator, or DRF permission class catches this before the response is rendered; the enumeration is confirmed and exploitable at the login endpoint.]

Missing rate limiting on password reset allows account enumeration and email flooding — Attacker can enumerate valid user accounts and flood inboxes with password-reset emails, causing denial of service to users and potentially exploiting the reset flow. [verified: password_reset_request at /accounts/password/reset/ triggers send_mail on every POST with no rate limit; email flooding is possible though the constant response message prevents user enumeration.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Password Reset (Email Bombing) — Attacker can flood any email address inbox with password-reset emails, causing denial-of-service for the victim's email and potentially hiding real security notifications. Also enables brute-force token submission against the password_reset_confirm endpoint. [verified: password_reset_request calls send_mail() unconditionally on POST at line 123-128 with no throttling; attacker can flood any inbox, though the always-identical response blocks enumeration.]

Webhook HMAC signing secrets stored in plaintext at rest — An attacker with database access can extract all webhook signing secrets and forge webhook deliveries to downstream services that trust the LMS, or replay captured webhook payloads. [verified: Webhook.secret is a plain CharField with no encryption at rest (confirmed: no fernet/encryption libraries in the codebase); the raw plaintext secret is read from the DB and used directly in hmac.new() at deliver_webhooks.py:70 to compute outbound HMAC signatures. Database compromise (backup exposure, read-only SQLi, insider access) would leak all webhook signing secrets, enabling signature forgery]

Missing Rate Limiting on JSON API Endpoints Enabling Denial of Service — Unrestricted API calls can exhaust database connections (key_prefix lookup per request) and application resources, causing denial of service. Combined with the SSRF through webhook responses stored per-request, an attacker can amplify server-side load. [verified: No rate limiting, throttling, or request-limiting middleware/decoration exists anywhere in the codebase (confirmed by grep); all four JSON API views are @csrf_exempt and each call triggers a database key_prefix lookup in _authenticate_api, enabling resource-exhaustion DoS via high-volume requests with arbitrary Bearer tokens.]

Reflected XSS via unsanitized 'copyline' parameter in course_blurb_card_004 — Arbitrary JavaScript execution in the victim's browser; session cookie theft, phishing, or malicious actions performed as the victim. [verified: `copyline` from request.GET interpolated into HTML served as `text/html` with zero output escaping, enabling reflected XSS.]

Reflected XSS via unsanitized copyline parameter in HTML response — If the internal ops token is compromised, an attacker can inject arbitrary JavaScript that executes in the victim's browser context. [verified: `copyline` from request.GET interpolated into HTML served as `text/html` with no output escaping, enabling reflected XSS.]

Open Redirect via lane parameter — course_return_lane_150 — Phishing attacks — attacker can craft URLs that appear to point to the trusted LMS domain but redirect victims to malicious sites, enabling credential theft. [verified: `lane` from GET/POST passed directly to Django `redirect()` with no allowed-host validation.]

Sensitive data exposure in logs — raw request body and Authorization header logged — API tokens, credentials, or PII written to application logs; log injection/forgery through newline characters in request body. [verified: Authorization header and request body logged in plaintext via `logger.warning`, exposing bearer tokens and sensitive data in logs.]

Sensitive Data (Bearer Tokens) and Arbitrary Content Written to Logs — course_wire_tally_211 — Disclosure of Bearer tokens/API keys in log files accessible to system operators; log injection attacks can forge log entries via newline characters in the request body. [verified: Authorization header and request body written to application logs in plaintext via `logger.warning`.]

Missing authorization — ops endpoint accessible without internal token check — An unauthenticated attacker can interact with this internal operations endpoint, violating the trust boundary. The endpoint could be used as an open proxy or for information disclosure if extended in the future. [verified: `course_identity_ping_334` has no `_wrk_gate` call, publicly accessible without the required x-internal-token header.]

Missing authentication on internal operations endpoint — An unauthenticated internal ops endpoint is publicly exposed. Input reflection could be used in limited cross-origin data exfiltration or fingerprinting scenarios. [verified: `course_identity_ping_334` has no `_wrk_gate` call, making it publicly accessible without the x-internal-token header.]

Hardcoded weak PINs for verification endpoint — The hardcoded 4-digit PINs can be trivially brute-forced (maximum 10,000 attempts) or discovered by reading the source code, bypassing any verification this endpoint is meant to provide. [verified: Verifier PINs `"4812"` and `"5930"` hardcoded in source; anyone with repository access can bypass the verification check.]

Permissive CORS — Mirrors Any Origin with Credentials — course_origin_mirror_370 — Cross-origin requests from any malicious website can include credentials; combined with other vulnerabilities, this enables cross-site request forgery and data exfiltration via CORS. [verified: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` mirrors the request's `Origin` header verbatim with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`.]

Permissive CORS configuration mirrors any origin with credentials — If the internal ops token is compromised, malicious websites can make authenticated cross-origin requests, potentially accessing sensitive data or performing actions on behalf of authenticated users. [verified: Origin header mirrored as `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, allowing credentialed CORS from any origin.]

CORS misconfiguration mirrors any Origin with credentials enabled — Attacker can perform credentialed cross-origin requests from any domain, potentially leaking sensitive data from authenticated sessions if combined with other endpoints. [verified: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` mirrors the request's `Origin` header verbatim and `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` is set, allowing credentialed cross-origin requests from any origin.]

Weak Pseudorandom Number Generator (random.choice) for Token Generation — course_nonce_roll_410 — Predictable tokens could be brute-forced or guessed by an attacker who observes a series of generated values, leading to token forgery. [verified: `random.choice()` from the non-cryptographic `random` module generates tokens instead of `secrets`, making output predictable given state observation.]

Denial of Service — unbounded string generation from user-controlled length parameter — An attacker can exhaust server CPU and memory resources by requesting large random strings, potentially crashing the application process or degrading service for legitimate users. [verified: `length` parameter cast to int with no upper bound; enormous values cause memory exhaustion and denial of service.]

SSL/TLS Certificate Verification Disabled for Outbound HTTPS Request — course_trust_drift_430 — Man-in-the-middle attacks on outbound HTTPS connections; intercepted or modified responses could feed malicious data back into the application. [verified: `ssl._create_unverified_context()` disables TLS verification for the outbound HTTPS request to the hardcoded partner URL.]

Disabled SSL certificate verification on outbound HTTPS request — Man-in-the-middle attacks against outbound connections — an attacker can intercept, read, and modify data exchanged with the partner endpoint, potentially injecting malicious responses or exfiltrating any accidentally-included sensitive data. [verified: `ssl._create_unverified_context()` disables TLS certificate verification for the outbound HTTPS request to partner.invalid.]

Weak authentication — trivially guessable cookie/header for authorization check — An attacker can trivially bypass the authorization check by setting a cookie or header to `"lead"`, gaining elevated access to the endpoint's response data which may include sensitive operational information. [verified: `badge == "lead"` uses a trivially guessable hardcoded string from cookies/headers with no cryptographic verification, enabling trivial bypass.]

Log injection — unsanitized request body and headers written to logs — Attackers can forge log entries, mislead incident response, obfuscate attack traces, or exploit log processing/viewing tools that interpret log content as commands or markup. [verified: `request.body` is logged via `logger.warning()` without newline sanitization, enabling CRLF log injection to forge log entries.]

Security headers (XSS-Protection, CSP) explicitly disabled — Removal of browser XSS auditor and CSP. Any XSS vulnerabilities in the application become easier to exploit against users who have visited this endpoint. [verified: Response explicitly sets `X-XSS-Protection: "0"` and `Content-Security-Policy: ""`, disabling browser XSS and CSP protections.]

Security headers weakened — XSS-Protection disabled and CSP cleared — Reduced browser-side protections against XSS and content injection attacks on the ops endpoint responses. [verified: `X-XSS-Protection: "0"` and `Content-Security-Policy: ""` explicitly disable browser security protections on the response.]
